FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford gave a frank assessment after the latest air traffic disruption. The nation's aging control system "will continue to break" until it is replaced, he said. He also named the companies working on the new architecture: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen. For AT&T (NYSE:T), the warning comes while the stock is down 6.36% year-to-date at $22.19. Over the same stretch, the business just posted its best consolidated service revenue growth in more than four years. Reaching $30 per share in 2027 will require AT&T to execute on several areas.

ninjaMonkeyStudio / Getty Images
Wall Street Already Sees 24% Upside for AT&T

Analysts' average target of $27.59 implies 24% upside. AT&T has beaten EPS estimates in six consecutive quarters. In the third quarter it earned $0.65 in adjusted EPS against a $0.60 estimate, and revenue rose 5.3% to $32.32 billion. Management raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to the $2.40 range and is targeting free cash flow of $19B+ in 2027.

An FAA foothold: AT&T already holds an FAA telecommunications modernization contract, including an initial $74.3 million task order awarded in August 2026. Congress previously provided $12.5 billion for air traffic control modernization, and officials are seeking roughly $30 billion more. Those are government-wide figures covering the entire modernization program, and each new task order would add long-duration revenue.

AI-grade fiber: CEO John Stankey noted that "over 90% of mapped U.S. data centers are within 10 miles of our fiber." AT&T is also working with Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) to meet its high-capacity needs.

Record customer growth: Internet net adds hit a record 769,000 in the third quarter.

Capital returns: AT&T plans $24B+ in buybacks from 2026 to 2028, and its $1.11 dividend yields about 5%.

Investors who want to avoid Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) but put capital to work in growth-focused, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) face a difficult challenge. Nvidia is an integral part of index funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) -- as the second-largest S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) and Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) holding behind Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL). Nvidia also joined the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) in 2024. And Nvidia carries an especially high weighting in many growth ETFs and tech sector ETFs.

However, there is a unique low-cost Vanguard ETF that doesn't own Nvidia yet still holds Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Apple, and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) as its top three holdings.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

A value ETF for the modern market

The Vanguard Russell 1000 Value ETF (NASDAQ:VONV) is a modern take on value stocks. While the Vanguard Growth ETF, Vanguard S&P 500 Growth ETF, and Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF label most major tech-focused companies as growth stocks, the Vanguard Russell 1000 Value ETF takes a nuanced approach.

The Russell 1000 is the 1,000 largest U.S. listed companies by market cap. It includes smaller large-cap and mid-cap stocks, whereas the S&P 500 just has large-cap stocks.

FTSE Russell, a subsidiary of the London Stock Exchange Group, has a semi-annual reconstitution whereby it roughly splits the market cap weighting of the Russell 1000 into two indexes -- the Russell 1000 Value Index (which the Vanguard Russell 1000 Value ETF tracks) and the Russell 1000 Growth Index -- which is mirrored by the Vanguard Russell 1000 Growth ETF. If FTSE Russell categorized all tech-focused companies as growth stocks, then the growth index would have a far higher market cap than the value index. So instead, FTSE Russell categorizes some established companies that were formerly high-octane growth stocks as value stocks, like Amazon, which is in the value index and not the growth index. Some stocks have their market caps split between both indexes. For example, Apple and Microsoft are top holdings in both indexes, whereas Nvidia, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta Platforms, and Tesla -- among other names -- are solely in the growth index.

As a result, the Russell 1000 Value ETF's three largest holdings are Amazon, Apple, and Microsoft -- which make up a combined 17.4% of the ETF as of Sept. 30. Normally, Apple and Microsoft would have higher weightings than Amazon because they have higher market caps. But since all of Amazon's market cap is weighted exclusively by the value index while Apple and Microsoft are split, Amazon is actually the largest individual holding in the Russell 1000 Value ETF.

Key Takeaways

IREN stock has lost 63% in the past year. Worries about debt-funded build-outs hit CoreWeave and the other AI cloud builders, and IREN's own build kept needing more money.

AI Cloud revenue nearly tripled to $200 million last quarter, but a Microsoft-requested design change helped push IREN's $4 billion run-rate target to January, and Nvidia, another big customer, lost its CEO.

IREN has paid for much of its build with stock: its diluted share count rose nearly eightfold from fiscal 2022 to fiscal 2026, and $6 billion of this fiscal year's build is still unfunded.

The stock trades at less than half its 3-year average forward sales multiple, but it's worth waiting to see IREN raise that $6 billion mostly with loans before buying more.

IREN (IREN:NASDAQ) stock has lost 63% in the past year and sits 74% below its June intraday high, even as its AI cloud revenue took off. The trouble is the bill for the build, and the two customers it leans on most, Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ) and Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ), both got more careful this fall.

Debt worries hit AI cloud builders in October, and CoreWeave (CRWV:NASDAQ) is down 32% in a year. But CoreWeave reported a $132.5 billion revenue backlog on Nov. 10, and IREN fell nearly twice as far, on problems of its own.

The growth showed up, a few months late

IREN's Nov. 5 report showed AI Cloud revenue nearly tripling from the June quarter to $200 million, and backlog reached $20.3 billion. A day earlier, The Information tied a Microsoft spending delay to IREN's Childress campus. IREN's release confirmed a delay: its $4 billion-plus run-rate revenue target moved from year-end to January, maybe February. On the call, co-CEO Daniel Roberts said Microsoft had asked IREN to "reconfigure and upgrade some of the network infrastructure."

title: Credo Technology Group vs. Marvell Technology: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
Credo Technology Group vs. Marvell Technology: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Sat, November 14, 2026 at 12:50 PM EST 6 min read
CRDO
MRVL
ORCL
MSFT
HG=F
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As demand for artificial intelligence continues to reshape the global data landscape, investors are weighing the explosive growth of Credo Technology Group (NASDAQ:CRDO) against the established dominance of Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL).

Credo specializes in energy-efficient connectivity for high-speed networks, focusing on specific bottlenecks in hyperscale data centers. Marvell offers a more diverse range of semiconductor solutions covering storage, optical, and computing needs across the entire networking ecosystem. Comparing these two reveals a choice between a high-growth specialist and a diversified infrastructure giant.

The case for Credo Technology Group

Credo focuses on designing high-speed copper and optical interconnect solutions that facilitate massive data movements within cloud networks. The company primarily serves blue chip hyperscalers and equipment manufacturers, with high-profile partnerships including Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT). Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as nearly 90% of revenue in its latest annual report came from just 10 customers.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached close to $1.6 billion, representing explosive growth of approximately 165.1% compared to the prior period. This rapid scaling helped the company generate a net income of roughly $538.3 million during that time frame. The resulting net margin of 33.8% highlights how effectively the company is translating its semiconductor stock sales into actual earnings as it expands.

As of its May 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio, which measures whether a company can cover its short-term debts with short-term assets, is 10.2x. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating a balance sheet with no total debt relative to shareholder equity. In the fiscal year ended May 2, 2026, free cash flow was approximately $407.0 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 39.3% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow in the cash flow statement.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell Technology provides the foundational hardware required to move, store, and process data across cloud and automotive markets. The company has a strong focus on the data center segment, which is increasingly driven by demand for custom silicon and high-speed networking. Marvell also maintains high customer concentration, as its top 10 customers accounted for roughly 82% of its revenue in its latest annual report.
